title: Relative perfection and endomorphisms of the affine adjoint unit
statement: Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions, and derived tensor pullback by K-flat resolutions. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $Y$ be an affine scheme and $f:X\to Y$ proper flat of finite presentation. Let $a_f$ be a right adjoint of $Rf_*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and set $W=a_f(\mathcal O_Y)$. Then $W$ is $Y$-perfect: it is pseudo-coherent (etale locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules) and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$ (tensoring with any module over that ring sheaf gives cohomology in a fixed finite interval locally). Moreover $H^i(Rf_*W)=0$ for $i>0$, and scalar multiplication is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(W,W)$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. Internal derived Hom here is the right adjoint to derived tensor product of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, lemma-properties-relative-dualizing, clauses (1)-(3); definition of relative perfectness: spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0DKN, definition-relatively-perfect.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $G=R\Gamma(X,-)$. Proper finite presentation over the affine base makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For a perfect $E$, ringed-site perfect duality gives $E^\vee$ perfect, $(E^\vee)^\vee\cong E$, and $E\otimes^{\mathbf L}W\cong R\mathcal Hom_X(E^\vee,W)$. The global trace adjunction, applied to $L=E^\vee$, gives the natural isomorphism $$T_E:G(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}W)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(G(E^\vee),A).$$ The perfect-sections theorem makes $G(E^\vee)$ perfect over $A$, and perfect duality on the one-object ringed site of $A$ makes its dual perfect. Thus $G(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}W)$ is perfect for every perfect $E$.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, first paragraph; derived global form of the displayed computation.

proof.text: The relative-perfection criterion applies to $K=W$: membership in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ is part of the supplied right adjoint, and $f$ is separated, flat and finitely presented. Step 1 supplies every perfect tensor test. Hence $W$ is $Y$-perfect and locally bounded below. In particular the internal-Hom quasi-coherence theorem applies to $K=L=W$: its source is pseudo-coherent and its target is locally bounded below with quasi-coherent cohomology. Put $B_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(W,W)$; it belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, end of first paragraph and last paragraph; local lower-bound hypothesis made explicit.

proof.text: Put $B=G(\mathcal O_X)$. Perfect sections with $E=\mathcal O_X$ make $B$ perfect over $A$, so a bounded finite-projective representative gives some upper Tor bound $N\ge0$. For every $A$-module $M$, the affine projection formula identifies $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ with $G(\mathcal O_X\otimes_A M)$: flatness of $f$ makes the pullback an ordinary sheaf in degree zero. Its derived global sections vanish in negative degrees, by the nonnegative injective resolution of a sheaf. Consequently $B$ has Tor amplitude in $[0,N]$. To apply the projective-window theorem, its pseudo-coherence hypothesis is obtained as follows: the proper flat structure-sheaf direct-image theorem makes $R\epsilon_{Y,*}Rf_*\mathcal O_X$ perfect on the affine Zariski site; its affine module preimage is pseudo-coherent. The Zariski-etale comparison, the affine module equivalence and the derived pushforward compositor identify that preimage with $B$. Thus the projective-window theorem supplies a finite-projective representative $P$ of $B$ supported in $[0,N]$.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, second paragraph, nonnegative Tor amplitude and finite projective model; Tag 0658 used through the existing projective-window node.

proof.text: Apply the global trace adjunction with $L=\mathcal O_X$. Since $R\mathcal Hom_X(\mathcal O_X,W)=W$, it gives $$G(W)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,A).$$ The right side is computed by $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,A[0])$ because $P$ is bounded projective. It is zero outside $[-N,0]$. The derived pushforward compositor gives $G(W)\cong R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*W)$, and $Rf_*W$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by the right-adjoint setup. Under the affine etale module equivalence, $\mathcal H^i(Rf_*W)$ is the associated sheaf of $H^iG(W)$. It therefore vanishes for $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, second paragraph, concluding vanishing argument.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:\mathcal O_X\to B_X$ be scalar multiplication, the transpose of $\mathcal O_X\otimes W\cong W$. For every perfect $E$, closed tensor-Hom adjunction, the supplied right adjunction, Step 1, and perfect biduality yield $$\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,B_X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(E\otimes W,W)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(G(E\otimes W),A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(G(E^\vee)^\vee,A)\cong H^0G(E^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,\mathcal O_X).$$ The last identification uses ringed-site perfect duality and the canonical global-Hom cohomology identification. These are natural bijections.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, third paragraph, Hom chain, written with H^0 rather than a derived object in a group-valued equality.

proof.text: Check the specified map in that bijection. A morphism $u:E\to\mathcal O_X$ corresponds by perfect duality to $s:\mathcal O_X\to E^\vee$. Under $T_E$, the trace functional of $u\otimes1_W$ is evaluation at the section $G(s):A\to G(E^\vee)$: both are $$G(E\otimes W)\xrightarrow{G(u\otimes1)}G(W)\xrightarrow{t}A.$$ Indeed the trace pairing defining $\tau_{E^\vee}$ first evaluates $E^\vee$ against its dual $E$, and evaluation on $s$ is exactly $u$ by the bidual triangle identity. Thus the inverse of the displayed bijection sends $u$ to the transpose of $u\otimes1_W$, which is $\alpha\circ u$. This proves that $\operatorname{Hom}(E,\alpha)$ itself, rather than an unspecified bijection of groups, is bijective. The argument also applies to every shift of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, third paragraph and scalar-map identification; evaluation-and-counit normalization of Tag 0E58.

proof.text: Take a distinguished triangle $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow\alpha B_X\to C\to\mathcal O_X[1]$. Its terms are quasi-coherent by Step 2. Bijectivity on every perfect test and its shifts gives $\operatorname{Hom}(E,C[n])=0$ for all perfect $E$ and all integers $n$ by the long exact Hom sequence. To use precisely the localizing-generation statement, fix $C$ and consider the objects $T\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(T,C[n])=0$ for every $n$. This class is closed under shifts, cones, retracts, and coproducts (Hom out of a coproduct is the product of Hom groups). It contains every perfect object, so localizing generation makes it all of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. Taking $T=C$ gives $1_C=0$, hence $C=0$ and $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Together with Steps 2 and 4 this proves all three assertions.

source.place: Tag 0E5V, final paragraph, generation applied to the cone.

lean.statement: theorem affineAdjointUnit_properties {S : Scheme.{u}} (Y : Over S) [IsAffine Y.left] (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace Y) (hproper : MapIsProper f) (hflat : MapIsFlat f) (hfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (schemeSpace Y).SmallModules] (F : QCohDirectImagePresentation f) (a : (schemeSpace Y).DerivedQCoh ⥤ X.DerivedQCoh) (adj : F.functor ⊣ a) : IsPerfectRelativeToScheme Y f (a.obj (schemeSpace Y).derivedQCohStructure).obj ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (schemeSpace Y).SmallModules i).obj ((derivedDirectImage f).obj (a.obj (schemeSpace Y).derivedQCohStructure).obj))) ∧ IsIso (derivedScalarEndomorphism X (a.obj (schemeSpace Y).derivedQCohStructure).obj)
lean.note: Canonical small affine etale ringed-model equivalence retains the original module universe. The actual scalar endomorphism map is fixed by the normalized closed tensor-Hom model; the direct-image presentation includes its natural identification with the canonical ambient K-injective Rf_*. Relative perfectness uses the equivalent affine etale chart criterion of 0DKN. Properness plus local finite presentation is finite presentation, since proper implies quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No mathematical statement correction.
